# Film journey scene: one drag crosses every window boundary

Parent: #15252 (the film epic; design record A3-M-06 [6091324649](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15252#issuecomment-6091324649) + the dialogue fold A3-M-06a [6091334597](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15252#issuecomment-6091334597)). Not blocked: #19533's fix landed on `dev` at 5698517f19 (PR #19539).

## Context

The operator's challenge on the film (2026-10-10 01:1xZ): the screenplay never shows the gesture's freedom. `film-tear-out`, `film-morph`, `film-second-window` and `film-reintegration` are four scenes of one hop each; the thing the engine does best — one drag that crosses every boundary as often as the hand likes while the pane keeps living — is never on screen. The journey scene is designed on the epic. Its hops 4–5 are #19533's B shape, shipped by PR #19539: inside a window of the group the drag is that window's tab-header proxy, outside every window it is a vessel; a claim retires the vessel riding the hand, leaving re-opens one (ADR 0029 §2.8.6). This ticket builds the runnable cue; the recorded take is the epic's AC-1 step ([6092305993](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/15252#issuecomment-6092305993)).

Live latest-open sweep: the latest 20 open issues at 12:57Z, no equivalent (#19537, #19538, #19540, #19541 are the dock cleanups; none touches the screenplay). A2A claim sweep: my own `[lane-claim]` of 12:51Z is the only claim on the film's cue. Memory sweep: the A3-M-06 design turn (session d6e132f0-fc2a-4d90-a3b5-5046668076e1); no earlier journey cue. Own-assignment sweep: #15252 (the parent) and #19382 (unrelated).

## The Problem

`apps/workstation/tour/fiveBeatFilm.mjs` is the narrative authority the in-app **Start film tour**, the whitebox replay and the recorded take all consume. Its window scenes are single hops: scene 3 `film-second-window` (the `convert-while-dragging` cue: Commits out → into Metrics' window → drop) and scene 7 `film-morph` (a `tear-out` cue with `reenter: true`: Metrics out → back → cancel). No cue walks the pointer through main, the desktop and a foreign window under one pointer-down, so the picture cannot show B.

## The Architectural Reality

- **Screenplay:** `fiveBeatFilm.mjs` — ten scenes summing to 97 s inside the 90–150 s envelope; `filmCueTypes` is the exact cue set the film uses; `film-second-window` (lines 162–187), `film-morph` (256–288).
- **Cue vocabulary and dispatch:** `apps/workstation/tour/cueVocabulary.mjs` (`WORKSTATION_CUE_TYPES`); `apps/workstation/view/TourController.mjs#executeCue` has one `case` per type, unknown → `false`.
- **Executors:** `apps/workstation/tour/NativeGestureDriver.mjs` — `executeTearOutStep` (arm, the progressive boundary exit, `waitForTearOutVessel`, the born hold, the `reenter` walk back to a point 35 % into the boundary rect, `waitForTearOutVesselRetired`) and `executeCrossWindowDockStep` (the client point frozen outside the boundary while the screen point travels, `readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot(...).ready` as the pre-release gate, `waitForCrossWindowTransfer`). The pointer is synthetic (`simulateEvent` with client and screen coordinates); the engine's claim geometry reads the screen point, so "desktop" is a screen point outside every window of the group (Demo B's `driveCrossWindowDesktopLeg` uses "below the source viewport" for the same reason).
- **Readiness contract:** `apps/workstation/view/CrossWindowGestureSnapshot.mjs#readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot` — with `draggedItemId`, `ready` requires the vessel gone (`!sourceVesselConnected`) and the target's proxy settled and visible in that window.
- **Witnesses:** `test/playwright/unit/apps/workstation/tour/fiveBeatFilm.spec.mjs` pins the scene list, the 97 s sum, births = 3, gates = 3, the `reenter` flags `[false, true]` and one born hold; `test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationFilmTourNL.spec.mjs` pins `totalBeats`, three continued gates, ≥ 3 popups born, the `convert-while-dragging` and re-entry receipts. `apps/workstation/README.md:59` still says "eight scenes".

## The Fix

1. **A `journey` cue** — `{type: 'journey', itemId: 'commits', sourceNodeId: 'right-bottom-tabs', targetItemId: 'metrics', hops: ['desktop', 'main', 'desktop', 'target', 'desktop', 'target'], options: {...filmPace, birthDwellMs: 1500, dwellDelay: 1000}}` — added to `WORKSTATION_CUE_TYPES`, dispatched by `TourController#executeCue`, executed by `NativeGestureDriver#executeJourneyStep`. Hops are data. `desktop`: a screen point outside every window rect of the group (computed from the Window manager, never a fixed offset); a fresh vessel must be born (`waitForTearOutVessel`, a window id different from the previous generation), then the born hold. `main`: the 35 % interior point; the vessel retires (`dockTearOutEntry` seen + `waitForTearOutVesselRetired`) and the committed document is byte-identical to the one before the gesture. `target`: the target vessel's centre in screen space until the snapshot is `ready` (vessel retired, the proxy in that window), then the dwell. The last hop is the drop: `mouseup` → `waitForCrossWindowTransfer` → the A+B adoption (`[metrics, commits]`), settled as `executeCrossWindowDockStep` settles it. Receipt: `{applied, errors, hops: [{kind, born|retired|claimed, windowId, …}], proof: {vesselWindowIds, documentsUnchangedAfterReturn, identityPreserved, sourceDocument, targetDocument, transfer}}`. A failed hop cancels the gesture (`cancelTearOutGesture`) and names itself in `errors`.
2. **The screenplay:** `film-second-window` → `film-journey` (the journey cue behind its gate, the captions of A3-M-06, `targetSeconds` 18); `film-morph` retired — its byte-identity pin is the journey's `main` hop. Nine scenes; the sum re-pinned (91 s, inside the band); the header's show-order prose and `filmCueTypes` follow (`convert-while-dragging` leaves the film's set; its executor stays for the five-beat witness).
3. **Witnesses re-pinned:** unit (scene list, sum, births = 2, gates = 2, `reenter` `[false]`, the hold on the journey); e2e (`filmCues`, two gates, ≥ 4 popups born and all closed by the signature, the journey receipt's hops and three distinct vessel ids replacing the `convert` and `reentry` blocks). README: nine scenes.

Decision Record impact: aligned-with ADR 0029 §2.8.6; no amendment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** `fiveBeatFilm.mjs` has nine scenes; `film-journey` sits where `film-second-window` was; `film-morph` is gone; the pacing sum is re-pinned inside the envelope; `filmCueTypes` names `journey` and no longer `convert-while-dragging`.
- [ ] **AC-2** `executeJourneyStep` walks the six hops under one pointer-down; its receipt records three distinct vessel window ids, the retirement at the `main` hop with the committed document byte-identical, the two `target` claims with the proxy inside Metrics' window, the final A+B adoption, and the same live pane across every hop.
- [ ] **AC-3** `WorkstationFilmTourNL.spec.mjs` green headless in both arms (viewer gates and `autoGates`): two gates, ≥ 4 windows born and all closed by the signature, the journey receipt pinned.
- [ ] **AC-4** `fiveBeatFilm.spec.mjs` green; the document tier still runs twice with identical logs.
- [ ] **AC-5** `executeCrossWindowDockStep` and the five-beat witness's scene 3 are untouched.
- [ ] **AC-6** The README's scene count and the screenplay header prose match the new order.
- [ ] **Post-merge (the epic's, not this ticket's):** the first headed take at this head after the operator's real-mouse check (#15252 AC-1).

## Out of Scope

The recorded take and Emmy's clips (#15252); the dialogue text (lives on the epic); the interactive tour's popup-permission prologue and the refused-open explanation (#19537, Emmy's); the dense tour; any engine change (#19538 / #19541 are Ada's deletions; nothing here depends on them).

## Avoided Traps

- A second copy of the tear-out executor: the hops reuse the existing waits (`waitForTearOutVessel`, `waitForTearOutVesselRetired`, `readCrossWindowGestureSnapshot`, `waitForCrossWindowTransfer`, `cancelTearOutGesture`); the executor is a hop walker over them.
- Driving the hops from the e2e with `page.mouse` (as `WorkstationHumanPopupOverlapNL` does for B's acceptance arm): the film plays from the app's own button, so the cue drives itself and the e2e witnesses the receipt.
- Keeping `film-morph` beside the journey: the journey's second hop is the morph; two scenes would show one hop twice.
- "Desktop" as a fixed offset past main's boundary corner: after scene 2, Metrics' committed vessel sits there.
